_comment: The guided tour. `accept` lists the commands that complete a step (the first words must match in order; flags anywhere); `run` is the exact command the guide offers; `where` is the side it runs on. Each CLI change updates the steps it affects (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
intro: # Welcome to Flint's demo. Nothing here is real: a demo vault lives in this page,
# nothing leaves your browser, and a reload resets everything.

hint: Your vault already holds a few hosts. List them. Flint first asks you, in its
window, to allow this terminal; the demo allows it for you:
Look at one. db sits behind a jump host; its password is stored, never shown:
Run one command on a server. The first time, Flint asks you to trust its key:
Copy a file to a server: the same login, over SFTP, with no key on disk. A folder
needs -r, an existing file needs --force, and alias:path on both sides copies
Open a shell on db. Flint goes through bastion for you:
You are on the server now. Look around, then leave:
Add your own server. Make up an address; the password is read with echo off:
Flint, the app, holds this vault unlocked; every flint command asks it:
Turn the demo vault into your real one: rename it. The file stays where it is:
Scripts and AI agents read the same vault as JSON:
A nightly job has nobody to approve it. Give it a token: Flint asks you in its
window (the demo allows it), then prints the token once, for FLINT_TOKEN:
steps.run: flint token create --name nightly --allow exec --hosts nas --ttl 30d

hint: A command as root: Flint's window shows you the exact arguments, and Flint types
the sudo password itself once you allow it (the demo does). The agent never sees it:

done: # That's the tour. Connect to the server you added, try --json (and | jq) on any command,
# or switch vaults with `flint vault use Work`. Type `tour` to start again.
